notes: Spawn prompt cited a fresh validation verdict (PASS WITH DRIFT) with three worst-deviation figures: Day 3 61.5% vs 67% (-5.5%), Day 5 61.5% vs 56% (+5.5%), Finale 39.5% vs 35% (+4.5%). Targets are the KITTED bands from vault/50-tech/verification-gate.md ('~84 / 93 / 67 / 75 / 56 / 72 / 63 / 52 / 52, finale ~35'); the checked-in pipeline/validation/report.md file on disk only carries history through the ui-integration-2026-07-29 cycle and does not yet contain this pass's full per-day table, so I worked from the three cited numbers plus the current kernel-panic-site/app/src/game/content/arc.ts values, per the launching agent's direct brief. Both deviations exceed the ~3pt noise band, sit on opposite sides of the target (D3 too hard, D5 too easy, no inversion between them), and I pulled the smallest lever (greed) before touching oppRam per the loop history's own finding that oppRam moves ~3-5 kitted points vs ~10 kit-less at this stage of the game, i.e. kitted closes end before opponent RAM matters. items.rationale: Report: Day 3 measured 61.5% vs the kitted target of 67% (-5.5%), a real wobble past the ~3pt noise band and the day's only deviation direction (too hard). Current day-3 greed is 0.88, already the sharpest step up from Day 2's 0.8 in the table. Greed is the smallest lever (per craft rules, ahead of oppRam and headStart) and Day 3 carries no oppRam headroom to spare relative to Day 4 (7 vs 7) without flattening the day-3/day-4 escalation. Dropping greed 0.88 to 0.84 eases the machine's per-rotation movement texture without touching oppRam, headStart, or grid, and keeps Day 3 below Day 4's 0.93 so the escalation still reads.

Report: Day 5 measured 61.5% vs the kitted target of 56% (+5.5%), the mirror wobble (too easy) and again past the ~3pt noise band. Current day-5 greed is 0.94, a full step below Day 6's 0.98. Greed before oppRam per craft rules; the loop history's Round 2 note ('oppRam +1 across D4-D8 measured only ~3-5 kitted points... kitted wins end before opponent RAM matters') argues against reaching for oppRam here since Day 5 is squarely in the kitted-fast-close band. Raising greed 0.94 to 0.97 tightens the day without disturbing oppRam (8) or headStart (2), and keeps Day 5 below Day 6 and Day 7's 0.98/0.99 so ordering holds.

items.idea: Finale measured 39.5% vs the kitted target of 35% (+4.5%), also past the ~3pt noise band and in the same 'too easy' direction as Day 5. I am not proposing a finale dayconfig-delta: per this agent's own lane fence, 'the finale and tutorial configs change only with explicit user sign-off,' and no such sign-off is in the brief or spawn prompt for this pass. If the user wants it pulled in, the smallest lever is still greed, but finale greed is already at 1.0 (the ceiling), so the next-smallest levers in order would be abilityFreq (0.9) or headStart (1), not oppRam or grid, once approved.
items.why: Flags a real, measured deviation instead of silently leaving it or silently touching a config this agent isn't cleared to move. Keeps the finale's escalation legible if a later cycle gets explicit clearance to touch it.

items.idea: pipeline/validation/report.md on disk ends at the 'Cycle ui-integration-2026-07-29' entry (bit-identical kit-less table, no kitted table for this pass). The three numbers this proposal is built on (Day 3, Day 5, Finale) came from the launching agent's spawn message, not from a table I could read in the file itself, so I have no visibility into Days 1, 2, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9 for this pass, only that they weren't named among the 'worst deviations.' Recommend the validation agent's next Write actually lands in pipeline/validation/report.md with the full 9-day-plus-finale kitted table (the report history shows this Write has silently failed to land twice before, at deep-balance-2026-07-28 Checkpoints A and D, both times caught and hand-landed by the Orchestrator) so arc-composer isn't proposing deltas for days it cannot see the numbers on.
items.why: Without the full table, a day sitting at, say, +2.9 (inside tolerance but close) is invisible to this agent and could tip past tolerance next cycle with no lever pulled in between. This is a process gap, not a curve gap; citing pipeline/validation/report.md's own gap history as precedent.
